summary: Ephemeral worker synchronization causing staggered 429s across SSE and batch routes
description:
Issue summary:
Streamlytics reports repeated 429 responses during a nightly ingest that mixes long-lived SSE telemetry streams with periodic batch uploads. The 429 waves appear staggered across us-east and eu-west and correlate with ephemeral worker churn during a scheduled job.

Impact:
- Customer reports 15% of SSE sessions receiving 429s intermittently for ~1-3 minute windows.
- Bulk import jobs report partial failures and increased retry loops.
- Business impact: ingestion backpressure and delayed downstream analytics for Streamlytics (dedicated pool).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id p-ded-04, prod-us-east primary with geo-failover to eu-west.
- Traffic mix: ~600 long-lived SSE connections + 40 orchestrator workers spawning ephemeral upload processes every 60s.
- Model route: open-llm-13B text-embed and chat endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start SSE telemetry stream at scale (500-700 connections) with keepalive pings every 20s.
2) Start orchestrator that spins up ephemeral upload workers in bursts on 60s intervals.
3) Observe rate-limit headers and 429 responses on SSE open-event frames and batch POSTs.

Observed behavior:
- 429s arrive in short, staggered waves at ~60s periodicity.
- Rate-limit headers show token window exhaustion with refill timestamps that are slightly different between edge and origin.
- Console shows quota usage spike for the tenant during the same windows, but total tokens consumed does not fully explain the peak (suggests double-counting or misattribution).

Expected behavior:
- No 429s for sustained, well-within-quota traffic; smooth refill accounting across ingress layers.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer-provided traces: sse-client-trace-20260310.log (attached by Streamlytics).
- Internal dashboards: tenant_quota_buckets, ingress-token-counts, edge-origin-latency overlays (see linked PR and Confluence runbook).

Initial mitigation requested by customer:
- Temporary increase of burst budget for dedicated pool and request to add jitter to orchestrator worker starts to avoid synchronized fanout.
investigation_notes:
03/10 15:40 UTC - Triage by SRE: observed matching periodicity at 60s in tenant quota windows.
03/10 16:10 UTC - Correlated edge logs: healthcheck/keepalive heartbeats from ephemeral workers align with preflight/OPTIONS calls from the orchestrator, causing token counts to increment twice in rapid succession.
03/11 09:20 UTC - Deep dive into rate-controller: discovered a race where ephemeral connection probe and origin preflight are both being counted against tenant burst pool due to missing de-duplication when probes originate from ephemeral pods behind pooled IPs. Edge emits refill timestamp A, origin emits refill timestamp B; mismatch led to short-lived perceived double consumption.
Hypothesis: synchronized ephemeral worker churn + pooled egress IP reuse + missing preflight dedupe leads to transient overcounting and refill-window misalignment, producing staggered 429 waves.
Data links: dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/tenant/streamlytics-quota?orgId=1, logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/q/streamlytics/2026-03-10.
Next steps:
- Apply short-term config change to edge to avoid counting OPTIONS/health probes against tenant burst pool (rolled to canary edge nodes).
- Add randomized jitter to ephemeral worker restart in orchestrator doc and recommend customer patch.
- Implement server-side de-duplication for preflight/probe accounting in rate-controller (tracked as follow-up task).
Owner: Marcos Rivera (SRE).

resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-03-10: edge canary to stop counting orchestrator OPTIONS/health probes (header-based filter) reduced spike amplitude.
Permanent fix: PR #87 in rate-controller implements request deduplication within refill window and normalizes refill timestamps across edge/origin. Backport approved and scheduled.
Customer follow-up: advised Streamlytics to introduce randomized jitter (recommended 5-15s) on ephemeral worker startup and to switch keepalive from 20s->30s for SSE to reduce alignment risk.
Postmortem items: create a small automated test that simulates pooled egress IP reuse + synchronized worker churn, add telemetry for preflight de-dup rate, and update runbook to include dedicated-pool probe exemptions.
Status: Under rollout. Expected full mitigation by 2026-03-14 after canary passes. Owner: Marcos Rivera.
